Hidden `/goal` evaluation no longer requires the session model's assistant text to be a raw JSON object.
On the Messages backend (cliproxy / DeepSeek), the verdict schema is advertised as the same `StructuredOutput` tool the agent already uses for tools.
If the model still leaks CoT or wraps JSON in a fence, the first `{...}` object is extracted before the strict schema parse.
If the session model still cannot produce a verdict, evaluation retries on `grok-4.6`, then `claude-sonnet-5`.
A DeepSeek flash `/goal` probe completed without `infra_paused` / invalid-JSON fail-close.
Stored session history stays in the unified conversation form, including provider-private reasoning blobs.
Each outgoing request is rewritten for the target API backend so Anthropic thinking signatures and Responses `encrypted_content` are not replayed to a model that cannot decrypt them.
Anthropic → Grok: drop Anthropic signatures, keep any plaintext thinking.
Grok → Anthropic: drop Responses encrypted blobs that Anthropic cannot accept.
Same-family continues leave encrypted blobs intact so the prefix cache stays warm.
Switching models no longer requires `/new` after a 400 `encrypted_content` mismatch.
Theme palettes live in `overlay-core`.
The structured workflow ACP wire contract lives in `overlay-workflow-control`.
Whole files authored by the fork stay under `overlay/` unless they are sanctioned `overlay_*` adapters.

Pre-existing enabling environment values cannot override the release policy.
Local diagnostics such as `RUST_LOG` and `GROK_DEBUG_LOG` remain available.
The overlay does not edit `~/.grok/config.toml` or install global hooks.
Every released built-in and CLIProxyAPI model has a cited effective context-window policy checked through the real runtime resolver.
